results.title: New GPU rates from October 5, 2026 | Jarvislabs Updates
highlights:
# New GPU rates from October 5, 2026

From October 5, 2026 at 00:00 IST, new rates apply to NVIDIA H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. They cover on-demand usage and any reserved plan started on or after that date. Current rates apply until then.

| GPU | On-demand rate until October 4 | On-demand rate from October 5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H200 SXM | $3.99/hr | $4.59/hr |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | $2.69/hr | $3.49/hr |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | $1.89/hr | $2.19/hr |

Rates are per GPU-hour, in USD, excluding tax, and apply in all regions. From October 5, the pricing page will list the new on-demand rates, including INR. For new reserved plan rates, contact us at engineering@jarvislabs.ai.

## Why rates are changing

A global shortage of GPU memory (HBM3e and HBM3 on the H200 and H100, GDDR7 on the RTX PRO 6000) has raised the cost of this capacity. The new rates reflect that cost.

## What isn't changing

- Committed nodes stay at their existing price for the full contract period.
- Storage rates are unchanged.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU-hour rates a second time. The memory line is where the story is · FLUX | EchoVerse Dispatches
highlights:
Nebius Group (Nasdaq: NBIS), an Amsterdam-based neocloud (a specialist cloud provider that leases Nvidia GPU compute to AI labs and enterprises), notified customers in September 2026 that on-demand, pay-as-you-go prices will rise October 1, with GPU-hour rates climbing 17–21% and the per-GiB-hour rate for Genoa memory on AMD EPYC CPU-only compute rising about 41%. It is the company's second price increase in roughly four months, and the size of the memory increase matters because enterprise budgets rarely hedge that cost the way they hedge GPU hours.

...

Nebius Group, the Amsterdam-based, Nasdaq-listed specialist GPU cloud, told customers in mid-September that on-demand On-demand (pay-as-you-go) Cloud capacity billed by the hour with no term commitment, at the provider's published rate. prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD EPYC Genoa CPU capacity and Genoa memory will rise on 1 October. It is the second increase this year. The headline is a GPU-hour hike of roughly 17 to 21 percent depending on chip generation. The more interesting line, four rows down the notice, is memory.

The details come from a customer notice reported by Shattered.io, with Reuters framing (via Yahoo Finance) attributing the move to demand outrunning supply. Nebius had not formally confirmed the changes publicly as of reporting. ⁠ 1 1 David Prior, "Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) Stock Price Hike Signals Surging Demand For AI Compute Capacity," Foreign Policy Journal, 19 September 2026. https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/2026/09/19/nebius-nasdaq-nbis-stock-price-hike-signals-surging-demand-for-ai-compute-capacity Treat every figure below as reported from that notice, not company-confirmed.

...

Foreign Policy Journal and Barchart, citing the same notice, report AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU-hours rising 25% to $0.015 from $0.012, and memory pricing tied to those Genoa systems rising roughly 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. ⁠ 1 ⁠ 3 3 Aditya Raghunath, "Nebius Stock Spikes 4% on Higher Computer Prices," Barchart, 22 September 2026. https://www.barchart.com/story/news/4740983/nebius-stock-spikes-4-on-higher-computer-prices-how-to-play-nbis-stock-here The CPU and memory figures have not been independently corroborated by a primary source; they should be read as secondary reports.

results.title: Same chip, three providers, three different answers to "what does this actually cost." | Compute Stacker
highlights:
On-demand H100, verified against each provider's own pricing page: CoreWeave $6.16/GPU-hour. Nebius $3.85. Lambda $3.99 (8-GPU tier). CoreWeave looks like the expensive outlier, roughly 60% above the other two.

That comparison is broken before it starts. CoreWeave's H100 rate is confirmed node-locked: an 8-GPU minimum, sold as a $49.24/hour node, with no self-serve single-GPU option. Nebius and Lambda both let you provision a single GPU at the same per-GPU rate. If your workload doesn't need 8 GPUs running simultaneously, CoreWeave's headline price isn't answering a question you're actually asking.

Spot pricing changes the comparison's shape entirely, where it exists at all. CoreWeave spot runs $2.46/GPU-hour, confirmed. Nebius preemptible drops to $2.15, a 14% gap from CoreWeave, not 60%. Lambda offers no spot or preemptible tier whatsoever, confirmed across its own pricing page and every independent tracker we checked. A workload that could tolerate interruption for a discount elsewhere is stuck at full on-demand rate on Lambda regardless.

One number worth watching rather than trusting as fixed: Nebius has reportedly announced a price increase taking H100 from $3.85 to $4.50, but as of our last check, that increase hadn't yet gone live on their actual pricing page. The $3.85 rate above is current, but treat it as a number in motion, not settled.

results.title: Nebius H100: $3.85 on demand, from $0.79 spot, September 2026
highlights:
On 2026-09-24 Nebius lists the NVIDIA HGX H100 at $3.85 per GPU-hour on demand, and preemptible H100 capacity from $0.79 per GPU-hour. Until the 06:39 UTC read of that morning our pages carried $4.50 as its on-demand rate and $3.85 as its spot rate. Both were real numbers on the page; neither stood in the column we thought we were reading.

...

What the page prints on 2026-09-24, read at 06:39 UTC: the H100 SXM at $3.85 on demand and from $0.79 preemptible, the H200 at $4.50 and from $0.79, the B200 at $7.15 and the B300 at $7.85, both from $0.99, the RTX PRO 6000 at $1.80 and from $0.79, and the L40S from $1.55 and from $0.74. The dated column is an announcement rather than a rate anyone can pay on 2026-09-24, so we publish none of it.

...

That read changed ten Nebius quotes at once, and our changelog carries them with both sides: the H100 SXM on-demand rate from $4.50 to $3.85, a change of -14.4%, and its spot rate from $3.85 to $0.79, a change of -79.5%; five more cards moved with them. Read as price moves they look like a deep cut by the provider on one morning. They are not: they are the distance between the column we read before and the column the heading names.

Two computed figures moved too. The Cloud GPU Price Index for the provisional week of September 21, 2026 reads $3.92 per GPU-hour on 2026-09-24; we read the same provisional week at $3.97 on 2026-09-23. And the spot discount band now runs from 81.5% below a provider’s own on-demand rate at its deepest to 20% at its shallowest, with a typical 50%, over 37 rate pairs at 6 providers. Read on 2026-09-23, the shallowest was 0%, over 42 pairs.

...

On our H100 SXM page the cheapest rate of any kind is now that Nebius floor, from $0.79 per GPU-hour, tagged high risk because preemptible capacity can be reclaimed mid-run. The cheapest on-demand rate is $1.79 per GPU-hour at Cudo Compute, 54% below the median rate card. Nebius’s $3.85 is a firm cell and its $0.79 is a floor, and the discount table never sets a floor against a firm rate, so the one Nebius pair it keeps is the L40S: from $0.74 against from $1.55, 52.3% apart.

results.title: B300 Rental Prices per GPU-Hour: Signed Contracts Since March 2026 · CCIR
highlights:
Eleven B300 rental contracts signed since March show three-year rates up about 25%, from $3.39 to $4.23 per GPU-hour. On a three-year contract for 10,000 GPUs, that move is about $220 million.

...

## 01 What prices did

- → Three-year rates: $3.39 to $4.23 per GPU-hour, up about 25%
- → Five-year rates: $3.30 to $3.77 per GPU-hour, up about 14%
- → Same provider: $3.45 in March on a three-year tenor, $3.94 in July on a four-year tenor

 Since March, seven listed companies disclosed 11 B300 rental contracts in their filings. The contracts cover about 31,000 GPUs and about $4 billion of contract value. 

 We fit a trend line to the rates and weight each contract by its GPU count. Three-year rates rose from about $3.39 per GPU-hour in March to $4.23 in August. That is a rise of about 25%. Five-year rates rose from $3.30 to $3.77, or about 14%. Two large contracts set most of the five-year line. 

 One seller shows the rise inside its own book. Boost Run rented 1,280 B300s for three years at $3.45 in March. In July it rented 1,536 for four years at about $3.94, on the same GPU-only basis. The July contract is also a year longer.

...

On a three-year contract for 10,000 B300s, the move from the March rate to the August rate is about $220 million. On a five-year contract for 10,000 GPUs, it is about $200 million. Both figures come from the trend lines in section 1.

results.title: Cheapest A100 Rental: 40GB vs 80GB Prices by Provider · Aliteq
highlights:
On Nov 12, 2026 a 40GB A100 rented from $0.32/hr on Vast.ai and an 80GB one from $0.81/hr (Lium; Vast from $0.84), against $1.35 on Hyperstack (Nov 3) and $1.79 on Runpod. Where the cheap A100s are, why 80GB costs about twice as much, and the jobs that need it.

...

The cheapest A100 rental is on Vast.ai's marketplace, and the memory size changes the price. In our read of Vast's offer API at 13:30 UTC on Nov 3, 2026, a 40GB A100 started at $0.40/hour on-demand (median $0.53 across 39 offers) and an 80GB A100 at $0.63/hour (median $1.00 across 25 offers). The cheapest 80GB card from a Vast-verified host was $1.00. Managed 80GB A100s listed at $1.35 on Hyperstack and $1.79 on Runpod Secure Cloud. Pay for 80GB when you run a 70B model, gpt-oss-120b or a 70B fine-tune; for 32B-class models and smaller fine-tunes, 40GB does the job for about half the price. Prices move every hour, so check today's live prices before you rent.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

The cheapest A100 rental on November 3, 2026 was on Vast.ai's marketplace: an A100 40GB from $0.40 an hour on-demand (median $0.53) and an A100 80GB from $0.63 an hour (median $1.00 across 25 offers; the cheapest from a verified host was $1.00). Managed 80GB A100s listed at $1.35 an hour on Hyperstack and $1.79 on Runpod Secure Cloud. Lambda and CoreWeave sell 80GB A100s only in 8-GPU machines, at $2.79 and $2.70 per GPU-hour. The 80GB card is worth its roughly double price when the job needs more than 40GB: Llama 3.3 70B at 4-bit (about 43 GB at 8K context by our estimate), gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI says it runs on a single 80GB GPU), QLoRA fine-tuning of a 70B model (41 GB per Unsloth) or 16-bit LoRA of a 32B model (76 GB). For 32B models at 8-bit with short context, or QLoRA up to about 40B, a 40GB A100 is enough.

...
